{{Short description|German mathematician (1882–1965)}}
'''Ernst Erich Jacobsthal''' (16 October 1882, [[Berlin]] – 6 February 1965, [[Überlingen]])<ref name="memorial">
{{cite web
|url = http://www.numbertheory.org/obituaries/OTHERS/jacobsthal_eng.html
|title = Ernst Jacobsthal
|last = Selberg
|first = Sigmund|authorlink = Sigmund Selberg
|language = English|date = 2006-10-27
|accessdate = 2007-10-05
}}
</ref> was a German [[mathematician]], and brother to the archaeologist [[Paul Jacobsthal]].

In 1906, he earned his [[PhD]] at the [[University of Berlin]], where he was a student of [[Ferdinand Georg Frobenius|Georg Frobenius]], [[Hermann Schwarz]] and [[Issai Schur]]; his dissertation, ''Anwendung einer Formel aus der Theorie der quadratischen Reste'' (''Application of a Formula from the Theory of Quadratic Residues''),<ref>

{{cite web
|url = http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=17980
|title = Ernst Jacobsthal
|work = [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]
|accessdate = 2007-10-05
}}
</ref> provided a proof that [[prime number]]s of the form 4''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 are the sum of two [[square number]]s. In 1934, he was fired from his professorship at the [[Technical University of Berlin|Technische Hochschule Berlin]], because of his Jewish origins. In 1939 he fled to Norway and became after the war a professor at the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in [[Trondheim]].<ref name="memorial" />
